messages.content: pretend you are a sass product pricing expert. My competitor offers a one time form filing service for $99 and an annual subscription that allows unlimited updates and filings for $149. Another competitor charges $149 for a one time filing and $249 for an annual subscription that renews each year. Assume the product are similar and commodities.  how should I price my service?

function.name: dynamic_pricing_calculate
function.description: Calculate the dynamic price for a product based on the IP address of the customer while ensuring the price does not fall below a minimum floor value. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

ip_address.description: The IP address of the customer, used to determine the geographical location for pricing adjustments.

base_price.description: The base price of the product before dynamic adjustments. This is a float type value.

price_floor.description: The minimum allowable price for the product after dynamic adjustments. This is a float type value.

pricing_factor.description: A multiplier based on the customer's location, used to adjust the base price dynamically. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning: We need to respond as a SaaS product pricing expert. Provide analysis of competitor pricing, market positioning, value proposition, cost structure, target customers, pricing strategy options (penetration, skimming, freemium, tiered). Suggest pricing tiers, maybe a freemium or free trial, then paid plans: one-time filing, annual subscription, maybe monthly subscription. Provide rationale: competitor's one-time filing ranges $99-$149; subscription $149-$249. Our product similar, so we can price competitively. We might consider offering a lower one-time price to attract new customers, but subscription price should reflect value. Could also offer a mid-tier plan with limited updates. Provide suggestions: $79 one-time, $129 annual; or $99 one-time, $149 annual. Also consider bundling, volume discounts, early adopter discounts. Provide guidance on how to test pricing, gather feedback, adjust. Also mention psychological pricing, anchoring, price elasticity. Provide steps: define value, segment customers, set price objectives, choose pricing strategy, test, monitor. Provide recommended pricing structure: Free tier (basic), Basic ($79 one-time), Pro ($129 annual). Or maybe a monthly subscription at $14.99/month. Provide explanation. Also mention competitor's renewal frequency: one competitor renews annually, other maybe monthly? Actually competitor 2 renews each year. So we can decide renewal frequency. Provide suggestion: annual subscription with auto-renew, maybe monthly option. Provide discount for annual vs monthly. Provide price points: $149 annual, $12.49/month. Provide discount for early adopters. Provide suggestion to use dynamic pricing based on location? But not necessary. Provide suggestion to use price floor.
